public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 181

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/181](https://www.erdosproblems.com/181)
- [Er93] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory*.
  Quaestiones Math. (1993), 333-350.
- [Ti22] Tikhomirov, K., *A remark on the Ramsey number of the hypercube*. arXiv:2208.14568 (2022).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos181

open SimpleGraph

/--
Let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph (so that $Q_n$ has $2^n$ vertices and
$n2^{n-1}$ edges). Prove that $$R(Q_n) \ll 2^n.$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_181 :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n : ℕ,
      (diagonalGraphRamsey (hypercube n) : ℝ) ≤ C * 2 ^ n := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos181

reformulations.difference: Lean requires one positive real constant bounding R(Q_n)/2^n for every natural n, including zero. Tikhomirov's Introduction states the conjecture asymptotically as R(Q_n)=O(2^n), with an absolute implicit constant.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A bound for all n implies the asymptotic bound. Conversely, enlarge an asymptotic bound's constant to cover its finitely many exceptional indices. Every R(Q_n) is finite and 2^n is strictly positive, including at n=0. A sorry-free Lean proof of the equivalence with Mathlib's IsBigO atTop compiled in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2208.14568 — v3 LaTeX source, especially the abstract, Introduction, main theorem and corollary, and notation section.
review.notes:
The file has one theorem and no additional variants or answer slots. The cube definition has the expected adjacency and vertex count; graphRamsey uses ordinary, non-induced copies in a graph or its complement. Finite Ramsey theory ensures its defining set is nonempty, so the natural-number sInf default is unreachable. Computed cube vertex/edge counts for dimensions 0–4 and proved R(Q_0)=1 and R(Q_1)=2 in Lean without sorry dependencies.

Source-access limitation: direct requests to erdosproblems.com/181 and the Er93 publisher full text were blocked by Cloudflare, so their complete remarks could not be inspected. The mathematical claim is explicitly stated in the accessible, cited Tikhomirov paper. The current companion problem database corroborates the recorded open status; no status discrepancy was found.
